alerts.title: Rising creatinine and declining eGFR on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF. Creatinine has progressively risen from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), with eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m². TDF is a known cause of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome. Evidence supporting drug attribution includes the steady temporal decline coinciding with 3 years of TDF therapy and proteinuria on urinalysis. Non-drug causes should also be considered. Occasional ibuprofen use (2-3 times weekly for 6 months) may contribute through NSAID-mediated renal haemodynamic effects. No diabetes or hypertension are present. The clinician's plan is blank, with no renal assessment documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess renal function trends, consider TDF substitution with TAF or AZT-based regimen, evaluate proteinuria, and review ongoing NSAID use.

alerts.title: Fatigue may signal TDF-related toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list exhaustion or extreme fatigue as a presenting sign of TDF toxicity including lactic acidosis and Fanconi syndrome. The patient reports mild fatigue over 2 months, attributed to work schedule. While the self-attribution and mild nature argue against drug toxicity, the concurrent renal decline (creatinine 1.4, eGFR 52) and proteinuria increase concern. Lactic acidosis and Fanconi syndrome are serious TDF complications that require evaluation. Alternative explanations such as anaemia (Hb 12.8, borderline low-normal) should also be assessed.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate fatigue with LFTs, RFTs, and lactate if clinically indicated. Consider TDF-related toxicity in differential diagnosis.
